shots.vo: You're on the ISS. Two hundred fifty miles above Earth, moving at *seventeen thousand* miles per hour.
Alarm: a *cloud of debris* is heading for the station.
This *really happened*: in twenty twenty-one, the crew hid in their spacecraft from the debris of a destroyed satellite.
You make it into the capsule. *Impact*… and contact with Earth is gone.
Every ninety minutes, a new sunrise. *Sixteen* a day.
And every ninety minutes, the station flies *through the debris* again.
You seal the hatches and move to another module. In twenty fifteen, an alarm like this *drove the crew out*.
Every day, the station sinks about *three hundred feet*. Engines push it back up — on commands from Earth.
Water comes from sweat and urine: the station recycles *ninety-eight percent*.
Your last hope: *ham radio*. Astronauts use it to talk to schoolkids.
You call Earth… and a radio amateur *answers*.
Undocking. Three and a half hours *to home*.
Seventy-five miles up, you hit the atmosphere. You are pressed into your seat: *four to five g*.
Parachute. Three feet above the ground, the *soft-landing engines* fire.
